summary: Every digit can independently change whether the alternating sums are equal, giving an Omega(n) inspection lower bound matched by the accepted one-pass scan.

optimality.argument: Starting from an all-zero balanced string, changing any one unchecked digit to 1 makes exactly one side's sum larger. A correct algorithm must therefore inspect every digit in the worst case, while the accepted implementation processes each digit exactly once.

replacement_checks.evidence: For every index, changing that digit alone in an all-zero string changes the answer from balanced to unbalanced.
The accepted implementation performs one conversion and one signed accumulation per digit.
Regression exhausts digit strings over 0 through 3 for lengths 2 through 6 and checks leading zeroes, odd and even lengths, and maximum-length balanced and unbalanced strings.
